newsitem.title: UK: IRAQI OIL BOOSTS MED TANKER CHARTERING RATES.
newsitem.headline: IRAQI OIL BOOSTS MED TANKER CHARTERING RATES.

text.p: A surge in expected liftings of Iraqi oil from the Turkish port of Ceyhan boosted chartering rates for million-barrel tankers plying cross-Med routes, shipbrokers said on Friday.

Rates for these ships were around 15 points up from the beginning of the week at around W90. Aframax 80,000 tonne tankers were little changed, however. This was illustrated by Repsol's fixture of the Sereno at W105.

The U.N. said Iraq's oil pricing formula for a second round of oil-for-food sales was formally approved on Friday and Baghdad is now free to submit oil contracts to U.N. overseers for the first time since the end of May.
Mideast/Asia rates for 250,000 tonne Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) were still firm as evidenced by Caltex's fixture of the 255,000 tonne World Prince to South Korea at W87.5.
Caribbean markets for 70,000 tonners were little changed, as were rates for Aframaxes crossing the UK/Cont region, which were trading at W97.5 on Friday.
